utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. We are Wednesday, the 23rd of April, 2008. I would like to welcome the members of the OTP and I would also like to welcome Mr. Seselj, as well as all the other people in and around the courtroom. Exceptionally today, we are in Courtroom number II because the other courtrooms were unavailable. This does not really have an impact on our case, because today's day is dedicated to video viewing, and this is going to be conducted in open session. The accused -- or the Prosecution, actually, is a chart for us. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. Good morning to Your Honours and to everyone in and around the courtroom. My colleague, Mr. Mussemeyer, will be dealing with the videos today, but we have circulated a list, and I'll turn the matter over to Ms. Mussemeyer for further discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. We have 15 video clips prepared for this morning. The first one -- the first six ones deal with the topic of a Greater Serbia, and the first video has the ERN number 6021. It has -- my case manager corrected me. The 65 ter number is 6021F. The ERN number is VOOO-3780. It's clip F. The Prosecution received this tape from the Croatian government on the 3rd of January, 2002, and it will last about one minute and 20 seconds. May I correct me [sic], it's not clip F, it's clip G.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I mean, it's a question of an artificial state under Tito, grotesquely created. It could only have been like that under communist dictatorship. Under natural conditions, the stronger one dominates. "Well, if Slovenia is now under the German domination?" "Well, I you can now if you'd rather have Serb or German domination. I think you would feel better under German domination. If nothing else, you will better. That is the most important thing for you, anyway. You all speak German. It is not hard for you." "Okay. That can --" "You will be Germany's seaside. "And where will you have a seaside? "As far as we're concerned we have Serbian seaside Temuci [phoen] to Karlobag. "And Dubrovnik? Dubrovnik is a Serbian city: "And which other one? For example, Split, Sibinik, Zadar, that these are all Serbian cities, I think that would be difficult." "You might think that it is difficult and you might be looking forward to the less fortunate others, if your primary goal is to make it more difficult for the Serbs, you're going to make it more difficult, but we are especially inspired by difficulties. We will achieve our goals, and then we will turn toward you and make you pay for making things difficult for us. Therefore, you should not be preoccupied by making it more difficult for Serbs, making it difficult for Macedonians, Croats, Siptars, Muslims. You should pay attention only to your own interests if you wish to achieve something."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise. The microphone was on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you check this out? There's a lot of interference. It's disappeared now, the noise. The first question poses itself here, and that's the relevance of the footage. The Prosecutor didn't emphasise that it was an interview to Slovenian Television and that it was Serbian-Slovenian relations and my advocating Slovenian independence. Now, here there's mention about the Serb cities on the Adriatic coast and how far the Serb part of the Adriatic coast stretches for, and then the Prosecutor should offer up evidence that that is not the way I put it, that that is not how I state it. I still state that from Utzim [phoen] to Karlobag is the Serb coastline. Now, the Prosecution is not leading any evidence against that, except the de facto state under occupation. First of all, there was communist occupation. Now we have American-NATO occupation. However, the situation is quite unnatural. So if you go back, revert to the natural situation, then the Serb coast will stretch to Karlobag, and we'll see what happens with Italy, what belongs to Italy in that area. But there's nothing Croatian there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your observations are noted on the transcript. Can we have the number, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Exhibit number 385.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: May I mention also that part of this interview has been published in Mr. Seselj's book. It's on the outline I gave to the Trial Chamber and also to Mr. Seselj. The second video again deals with a Greater Serbia. It has the 65 ter number 1836C. The ERN number is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection before the next footage. It's not that one part of this interview was published in my book. The interview in its entirety was published in my book. I don't have the attachment here. By mistake, I brought in the previous piece of paper, because when I moved, all my documents got mixed up, but I can remember them and tell you from my head all this was published in my book in its entirety, not just a portion of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber notes that the entire interview conducted with the Slovenian reporter is published in your book, which was published in Belgrade in 1993, according to the document presented to us by the Prosecutor. Please go on. The.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I continue with the second clip. It's again under the topic Greater Serbia. It has the 65 ter number 1836C. It has the ERN number V000-0278. It's about one minute and eight seconds long. It was broadcasted in May 1993, and the tape was received from the Serbian TV a long time ago, and we don't know -- we cannot exactly identify when and where we got it from, but we got it from the Serbian TV.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "And in -- on the other hand, things will be developing in the completely opposite direction to what Slobodan Milosevic experts and what Alija Izetbegovic expects. There will be no Muslim state in the area of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina. Bosnia and Herzegovina will be divided into the Serbian and the Croatian part. I can draw you now a sketch of the border where it will be carried out: That is, Zvijezda Mountain in Central Bosnia towards somewhere around Zavidovici. I cannot say precisely whether Zavidovici would be on the Serbian or Croatian side. Approximately here. The Olovo-Maglaj line will be completely in Serbian hands, and the border with Croatia will be around Travnik and then will lead towards the line of contact from the north, between Republika Srpska and Herceg-Bosna. There will be more complication from the south, of course, in the area of the Neretva Valley and the exit to the Adriatic Sea, but it is possible that these issues will be resolved in the course of negotiations. Nothing will remain of the Muslim state because Europe does not want to see a Muslim state on its own territory, and it will be proved that the Muslims are the greatest victims of this war. Reason for all that is their stupidity and the belief that someone from abroad would be willing to create a state for them."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the technicians playing the tape are not turning off the apparatus. I think that's why I am receiving interference. Once again I raise the question of relevance here. I am presenting a very truthful fact here, that Europe doesn't want to see a Muslim state, that Europe and America have decided that the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croats be held as hostages in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there's some nonexistent Bosnia-Herzegovinian state, whereas it's clear to everyone that a state like that can only exist while it is under foreign occupation. As soon as the foreign troops are withdrawn and the foreign governor, which is called the high representative, then the state will disintegrate and might enter into a civil war once again. So the question is : What does the Prosecution want to achieve by presenting this footage? I am presenting truthful facts, and the Prosecutors are surprised that I'm not saying that, that I'm not saying all the stupidities that western politicians say, that Bosnia-Herzegovina will remain as a state, that it will be equitable with other states, that it will be a unitarian state and that constitutional reforms will take place, it will have a united police and army and so on. As long as there's coercion and it's under that coercion, it exists, but when it disappears, the state will disappear. So what does the prosecution wish to show and prove by showing this footage? The prosecution is proving nothing. It's saying to you, Judges, this is the what he's like, that's the kind of man he is. And I'm very proud of being that kind of man. And what's relevant as far as the indictment is concerned is nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Before I ask Madam Registrar for a number, I would like to make an observation. The footage that we just saw, according to the Prosecutor's document, is a discussion in a group, or we saw Mr. Seselj -- we see Mr. Seselj on the screen, but Mr. Tomislav Nikolic was also present at this discussion, as well as Mr. Aleksandar Vucic, and there was a fourth person, Nikola Poplasen, who was equally there. I also note that the footage and -- the footage belonging to this video starts with the word "the." Mr. Seselj, actually, answers a question that we do not hear. We do not -- what was the question put to him, and he gives an answer. He says, "Yes," and he goes on. So this is an observation on my part. Madam Registrar, may we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, if possible, could you tell the Prosecutor to provide me with a copy of the list, and then I can help out and identify the footage on the video if I have it in front of me, because I wasn't really able to find that piece of paper. I was moved on Monday again, so I wasn't able to find that latest list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You will be provided with this document, but could we have a number first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become exhibit number P386.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I address myself to the prosecution. You also prepared a document for the transcript. Would you be able to print in B/C/S and in English this document and to hand it to Mr. Seselj, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. We will have to wait a minute that it will get printed. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we can continue. There's no problem there. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's proceed with video number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Video number 3 is 65 ter number 1836D. It has the ERN number V000-0278. It's about a minute long. It deals with visit of Professor Seselj to Glogovica, close to Sarajevo, and it took place the 14th of May, 1993. We received, again, this tape from the Serbian TV a long time ago. Like the former one, we cannot identify when exactly we got this video clip.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Well, the Serbian people of Republika Srpska and Serbian Sarajevo hold a referendum, I am convinced that they unanimously decided to reject the Vance-Owen Plan, and the Western forces should know that the Serbian man will not surrender here, that the Serbian man will never capitulate. The Serbian people are in favour of peace, we insist on a truce and the peace plan, but if someone wants sincere peace, then it should be agreed that borders be put at front lines. This is the only way. And if foreign military intervention takes place, thousands and thousands of members of interventionist forces will get killed here, and we will bring thousands of volunteers in from the other side of the Drina River, bring our brothers, Russian volunteers, and take Sarajevo by storm and liberate it."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, the problem of relevance. First of all, it is true that I was against the Vance-Owen Plan and it fell through, so what does the Prosecution intend to prove with that? That I'm always against Western forces and against NATO? Well, that's quite true, yes, I am always opposed to them. So if that's the subject of the indictment, you needn't hold a trial anymore. I am against the European Union and certainly of NATO. That's the first point. The second point is if there is foreign military intervention here, then I say so many people will be killed, members of the invasionary forces, and that we will send in volunteers and call up Russian volunteers and all the rest of it and that we will take Sarajevo by storm. So if there is foreign military intervention, that's something we can do too, but where's the relevance there as far as the indictment is concerned? Once again, they're working according to the principle, "see what kind of man he is," and I told you in advance that I agree that you proclaim me the worst man in the world, and I acknowledge that, I'm ready to acknowledge that, that I'm the worst man in the world, but I want you to prove that I committed a crime, and you cannot do that, because although I am the worst man in the world, I have not committed a crime, and this deals with nothing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we get a number, please, for this exhibit, for this video clip. Your commentaries are in the transcript. You say that this document is not relevant. The Trial Chamber will judge for itself. What is the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number 387, P387.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The next video clip deals again with a Greater Serbia. It's only 15 seconds' long. It has the 65 ter number 6048A. The ERN number is V000-1516. It's clip A. We received this video from the AID Sarajevo agency. I'm not aware when we got this, but maybe that I can tell you later. Let's play the clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Before we play this footage, Mr. Mussemeyer and Mr. Mundis, I noted in the opening statements that there were some reference to the videos, and I have to tell you, in your pre-trial brief, you mention that. I don't know if the videos you are presenting today are in the pre-trial brief. If some of the footage figure in the pre-trial brief, in the footnotes, you should tell us so that we can be even more attentive while viewing this footage. I did not check this time, but you should be able to know if these video clips that are shown are mentioned in your pre-trial brief. If that is so, please tell us. Very well. And so under reserve, we will look at the footage now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I may add I found when we got this document, it's the 1st of July, 1998, and the submission date was the 27th of August, 1998. That is what I can add. I'm not in a position at the moment to tell you which of these videos were mentioned in the pre-trial brief. I can do this later. I must check. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The Serbian radicals will never give up on the Western Serbian border, and one day we will realise the Karlovac-Virovitica line as the Serbian border."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the Prosecution here is trying to prove indubitable facts. Why is the Prosecution trying to prove that when it's not challenged? I said that in my introduction. I confirmed that by cross-examining that alleged witness, French member of the intelligence service, alleged expert. That's indisputable, and now the Prosecution is amassing evidence for this indisputable fact. If you just want to fill in the time, I understand them, then. They have no witnesses today, no witnesses tomorrow, so let's fill the time up with something. That's all we're doing here. They're not able to prove anything. Greater Serbia is the longest political programme of the Serbian Radical Party. It will go on after my life, probably my successor's life. There's a primary programme, there's a medium stage programme, but it's the most long-term programme of the Serbian Radical Party, and I explained to you what it means. It means making the Serb Catholics and the Serb Muslims more aware of themselves, eliminating foreign influences, the Vatican, America, the European Union, and so on and so forth. But what does the Prosecution want to prove by this, something that is not challenged in the first place, that is indubitable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I have two problems. One is a technical problem. I can never hear the end of the interpretation of what you are saying in the footage because you start intervening while the French interpretation is still going on. The second thing. I would kindly ask you to limit yourself in your comments. Allow us to work as well. The Trial Chamber must also work. You are substituting, with your commentaries, the evaluation of the Trial Chamber. Try to be a little bit more succinct in your comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please get a number, Madam Registrar. One moment, please, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Exhibit number is P388.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely have no intention of depriving the Chamber of any right, and how can I deprive the Chamber of any rights? There's nothing I can do to the Chamber. You can do everything to me, because I'm in your hands. I can do nothing to you. All I can do is to verbally oppose you, but in this way I'm drawing attention to the fact that you do not have the same criteria to the offered evidence by the Defence and the evidence of the Prosecution. It is already evident that you are prone to filling the files with irrelevant evidence of the Prosecution, and the important evidence that I offered at the beginning, you rejected, so I'm not offering any further evidence. So that is the gist of it. Do we need to encumber the case with irrelevant and superfluous evidence? Do we need in the proceedings to prove something that is undisputed? If it is undisputed between the Defence and the Prosecution, and that is the concept of a Greater Serbia, which is the long-term programme of the Serbian Radical Party, everyone knows that, why do we need to prove it? If that is the only way to fill in the time so that the trial should not be in a crisis, then I understand. We're doing all this to fill in the time. But if -- I don't understand that it is really indispensable to include this in the file. My comments are very brief, and I am focusing only on the gist of what is being offered here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's view the following video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The topic of the next two videos is again Greater Serbia, but there is a specific link to Bijeljina. Bijeljina is a municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it's a removed municipality, but the Prosecution is allowed to lead pattern evidence. That is the reason we are playing these two videos. The first of these video has the 65 ter number 6048B. The ERN number is V000-1506. It's about one minute and 30 seconds' long. It deals with Mr. Blagojevic, who was a vojvoda or who was appointed vojvoda by Mr. Seselj in 1993. We got this tape from the AID Sarajevo agency. Maybe that I can -- yeah, the date is the same like the video we showed before. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Did you expect war to break out in Bijeljina?" "Well, the war, although we had -- I had at that time already established the board of the Serbian Radical Party here, and according to our analyses and our views, war was inevitable. We undertook a massive campaign to prevent the war from breaking out. We called on our Muslim brothers not to allow themselves to be the object of external manipulation, to be manipulated by the Croats, Austria and Germany, for they would only lose what they already had. Our words, however, went unheeded, and what happened was the war started. "There is, in fact, a communique here, released on the 15th of October, 1991. It was precisely here that we, the Serbian Radical Party for northeastern Bosnia, appealed on the leaders of all political parties, both parliamentary and non-parliamentary ones, to continue to seek a peaceful political solution while there was still peace, for in wartime and after war, no solutions would be suitable to anyone. But that is as it may be. "The way things stand now, we shall certainly get a state of our own in this territory. The Muslims will never get one. For we have nothing against them getting a state of their own, but I know for a fact that the West does not want any kind of Muslim state on the soil of the Balkans or Europe."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One question for Mr. Mussemeyer. Mr. Blagojevic, who exactly is he?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: He is the local leader, if I may say so, of the Serbs in Bijeljina. He was appointed vojvoda by Mr. Seselj. I think it was the 13th of May, 1993. We saw videos about this in former sessions, and he is responsible for Bijeljina. And as the Prosecution thinks, he took part and organised the takeover of Bijeljina by the Serb forces in the end of March, beginning of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Blagojevic" is a very common name, Mr. Prosecutor. Do you know the first name of this person, the surname?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Blagojevic, and Mirko is the first name. And if you want to read, I think you'll have to go to the order of Mr. Seselj. The number is 124, where he was listing all the vojvodas at that time, and there appears also Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mirko Blagojevic is today a president of the Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska. He's a prominent Serb patriot. In the last term, he was a national deputy in the federal assembly in Sarajevo. I don't know exactly which chamber. Now, what does the Prosecution wish to offer with this clip? What is relevant here? Mirko Blagojevic is presenting a political thesis. Is that prohibited, is it wrong? This can only be exculpatory material, because it is true that we Serb radicals persistently, as soon as the war broke out in Croatia, called on the Muslims for peace, for avoidance of bloodshed, avoiding a conflict, avoiding the secession of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because it was quite clear to everyone that if secession occurred, war would break out. What does the Prosecution want? I see that the Chamber is not raising the question of relevance. That is why I'm doing it. Of course, I don't expect you to accept my objections, but in the interests of the public, I think it is necessary for me to make those objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely not, Mr. Seselj. Everything you say is very carefully heard by us. It is checked, all transcripts, the French transcripts and the English transcripts. As an example, too, something really struck me from what you just said. The person being interviewed is talking about his Muslim brothers, and, secondly, he's also saying that he set up the council of the Serbian Radical Party for the north or west of Bosnia; I can't really remember. But this is not pointless, and we will now give this footage a number, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video will become Exhibit number P389.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next footage, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next video deals again with Mirko Blagojevic and with Bijeljina. The topic is again Greater Serbia. It has the 65 ter number 6048C [Realtime transcript read in error "6548C"]. The ERN number is V000-1056. Again, the source where the OTP received this video is the same like before, it's the AID of Sarajevo agency. And the clip is about one minute and 29 seconds' long.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "You have identified yourself as a member of the Serbian Radical Party. What are your views on the current situation?" "Right now, the radicals' opinions are those that the people readily understand. We have a clear programme and objective. We are fighting for a Greater Serbia. There is no --" "Does a Greater Serbia exist?" "A Greater Serbia does exist, and it has been created." "Where are its borders?" "Now the borders run parallel with the front lines." "Is there a border on Drina and should there be one?" "Well, I am greatly pleased to hear these signals, that the sanctions against Serbia will be lifted. I would like that. Serbia has shouldered, it has paid a high price for our freedom and our state. There is no frontier on the Drina nor will there be one. This current blockade will also be short-lived. It is porous, and, in any case, Serbia will not let us go hungry. Only in the event that Serbia should go hungry, then we'll be very hungry, very hungry indeed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. It is the same as the previous one. A politician, a prominent politician of the Serbian Radical Party, is presenting his views, and what is incriminating in this opinion? The Prosecution is not offering anything incriminating. It is offering a document without any substantiation. If it is meant to be incriminating, it should be linked to the indictment issued against me. These are two things that are absolutely vague. It is even unreasonable to offer something like this into evidence without any explanation. Mirko Blagojevic is a reputed politician. He presents the views of his party, his personal views. What is the problem there? He's making that statement in 1994, outside the framework of the indictment against me. You have heard that he already mentions the blockade on the Drina that Milosevic and the regime in Serbia imposed. What is relevant there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mussemeyer, I see in the transcript that it is on page 16, line number 23, that the 65 ter number is referred to as "6548 Charlie." Is that the correct number or was it 6048?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: It's 6048C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Let that be corrected in the transcript. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's give a number to this, and I will make a brief comment on this afterwards. Ms. Registrar, could we please have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Exhibit P390.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My comment deals with the relevance which is challenged by Mr. Seselj. The witness -- not the witness, but the person interviewed talks about Greater Serbia. Fine. Greater Serbia is mentioned in the indictment. Secondly, he's also saying something that could prove very interesting, and I quote exactly what he said: "Borders are parallel to the front lines." So this is a sentence that could prove extremely interesting. The second thing regarding relevance: This person is in charge of the Serbian Radical Party, and he is speaking. In the Serbian Radical Party, there's a president, there are other people at different levels, and here we have a leader at a certain level speaking out. This can be quite interesting to hear this kind of person giving his opinion on a number of elements. Now let's continue, please, Mr. Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have an additional objection. In that case, the Prosecution should provide tapes of all the statements of high officials of the Serbian Radical Party, because all of them are advocating a Greater Serbia. The entire membership of the Serbian Radical Party is advocating a Greater Serbia. This is an undisputed fact. Someone who is not advocating a Greater Serbia could not be a member of the Serbian Radical Party. Should somebody appear as a member and present a defeatist thesis that Greater Serbia is impossible, he would be expelled from the party. So I don't know what the relevance is. And bear something else in mind, please. The Serbian Radical Party is registered in Serbia. The Serbian Radical Party of Republika Srpska is registered in Banja Luka. These are two separate parties which share the same ideology. They cooperate amongst themselves. They even have coordinating bodies, but they are two separate parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All the more so that you should talk about this difference, the fact that there is two political parties, one that is registered in Banja Luka and the other one in Belgrade, two parties sharing the same ideology, but who legally are two different entities. And this is now on the record. Mr. Mussemeyer, you have the floor for the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: In the meantime, I could check our records and have additional information related to Mirko Blagojevic. I referred already to the order number 124 from Mr. Seselj. This order dates the 13th of May, 1993. It has the exhibit number 1841, and Mr. Blagojevic is mentioned under number 2 in this order. So if there's any need to read or to get more information, it's possible to find it from there. I come back to the next two videos. We change a topic. It's now recruitment of volunteers. The ERN number is -- the 65 ter number is 6008C. It was -- on the outline you got, there's a typo. You got "6008A." It should read "C." The ERN number is V000-4260. The clip was taken in the fall of 1991. It's about two minutes and eight seconds' long, and the OTP received this clip from a protected witness. I will not mention the name. We do not receive any translation. There's a sound behind. Maybe we have a technical problem which has to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was no sound. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play it again?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This is the fourth group sent to the battlefield." "How do volunteer detachments cooperate with Yugoslav People's Army? Under whose command are they? "The volunteers who are being sent to the hot spots in Croatia by the Serbian Radical Party have exceptionally good cooperation with members of the Yugoslav People's Army. There are no more ideological obstacles today, and we believe that the Croatian fascist authorities are currently the only obstacles for the Serbian people in Croatia, the Serbian people in Serbia, and the Yugoslav People's Army, and I think that we can handle them. All the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party are under the Territorial Defence command and in joint action with the Yugoslav People's army units, they are liberating Serbian land. "The response is quite big. When is the next due to group leave? "The next group will leave as soon as we get the confirmation that these ones arrived safely. "Do you already have new requisitions? "We have new requisitions, indeed, and these days we plan to send somewhere between 800 and 1.000 new volunteers, especially to Western Slavonia before the end of this month. "This is unusual in the battlefield. What is your attitude towards that? "I think it is not and that we should all respond to this call. I am also the mother of two underage children. "Where are you from? "From Pirat. "How old are you? "Thirty-three. "How did you decide? "Well, when I watched television, I see what is going on and I want to help, and this Serbia of ours is worth sacrificing your life for. "Who stayed with the children? "Daddy stayed. That was the deal. "Daddy stays, momma goes. "Yes. "That is a bit unusual as well. "Well, it is. But that's me and I want to go. "What do you expect there? Are you not scared?" "Well, I am not now. I shall see. I expect us to win and to come back. "With a rifle in your arms? "Well, yes. "Have you ever held a rifle? "As a high school student, that time when we went for target practice. Next groups of volunteers will be leaving from the 4th of July military barracks in Belgrade, where they will be selected; before that, trained shortly and get uniforms."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is exculpatory material. The statement of Ljubisa Petkovic, the chief of staff of the Serbian Radical Party, that all the volunteers were part of the Territorial Defence under the Yugoslav People's Army. The Prosecution has confirmed that the Territorial Defence was under JNA command, so I don't see what is being proven here. Volunteers are in civilian clothes. They need to go to the barracks to pick up their uniforms. I'm glad that you are showing this video, because it recalls my -- reminds me of those glorious times. But what is relevant here, what is being proven here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Number, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number P391.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer, before we proceed, I would like to tell something to Mr. Seselj. He ended a sentence by saying, "What is relevant here?" I absolutely do not understand this comment. What is relevant, in the interests of justice, is to have the evidence and the elements that will help Judges rule on matters that are in an indictment. All these elements that we are seeing are -- is available evidence and elements that will help Judges assess the situation. If this video had not been admitted, we would not have known that the volunteers were going to the 4th July barracks, where they were handed uniforms and weapons. We would not have known that they were under TO authority, which was collaborating with the JNA, and we would not have known, and here I quote the person answering the reporter, we would not have known that there had been dissent between the Serbian Radical Party and the JNA, and that as of now, and I quote again this person, "There is now no more barrier," adding that the main barrier were the Croats. That's it. If you don't want to have this type of video admitted, it's fine for you, but this would be absolutely impossible to understand for us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't say that I didn't want it to be admitted. On the contrary, I said that it was exculpatory material. I must make a correction. The chief of staff didn't say that he was fighting against the Croats, but against the Croatian Ustasha regime. That was his statement; maybe not literally, but he's referring to the Ustasha regime. And the third point: We had a large number of evidence produced so far about all this in the proceedings up to now, that there were problems with the JNA in the beginning, when the JNA was neutral, even more prone to support the Croats than the rebel Serbs, that the volunteers had to cross the Danube in secrecy, et cetera. And that cooperation improved in September. All this has been established during the proceedings. So in this way, we are amassing more evidence than has already been presented and was confirmed. Of course, if that is what you wish to do, I don't mind. I'm glad that this is being viewed, but I have to make an objection. In fact, you have asked me to do that. I did my best to make them brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given that it seems that the -- what the person interviewed is saying is being challenged, because you say he talked about the Ustasha Croatian regime. I thought he spoke about the Croats. I think it would be best to play it again and listen to it once more. That way, we will be sure to know exactly what was said. Could we play again just the very beginning of the video, because it's at the very beginning that the interviewer is talking about this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This is the fourth group sent into the battlefield. How does cooperation between the volunteers detachment and the Yugoslav People's Army developed and under whose command are they? "The volunteers which the Serbian Radical Party sends to crisis areas in Croatia is cooperating extremely well with members of the Yugoslav People's Army. Today, there are no ideological obstacles, and we believe that the Croatian fascist authorities are currently the only obstacle for the Serbian people in Croatia, the Serbian people in Serbia, and the Yugoslav People's Army members, and I think that we can handle it. All the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party are under the Territorial Defence command."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Mr. Seselj is right. The exact words are "the Croatian fascist authorities." This is exactly what I heard.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is right. And may I also add, since I viewed it again, you mentioned misunderstandings with the JNA. Ljubisa Petkovic is clear in what he says. The previous ideological problems have been overcome, because it used to be an orthodox communist army, the red army in the proper sense of the word. Do you remember, we had figures here when a valley was organised in front of Tito's mausoleum, that the army wanted to attack us because of that, but things had changed. The army was no longer Orthodox communist, not to a sufficient extent, in our view, but it had changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move on to the next video, now that everything has been cleared up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The next video is again under the topic "Recruitment of volunteers." It bears the 65 ter number 6008B. The ERN number is V000-4260. It's about one minute 20 seconds' long, and the source is the same as the last video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "These are the volunteers from Serbia, about 50 of them, including three women, set off from Belgrade around noon today towards Slavonia and other hotspots in Croatia. Young men but also the elderly from Belgrade, Smederevo, Raska, and other cities are going, as they have just said, in readiness to help the Serbs in Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem, wherever is needed. "The youngest child is 13 years old, a girl, and she will take care of her brothers. I believe I can help and I want to help so that my children and those other children could continue to live in peace. "My son is going there because he's Serbian and because he's having a hard time watching the Serbian people suffering over there. "Are you the son? "I am the son. "Why are you going? Let me hear it from you. "I'm going there for the Serbian people and for Serbia. I believe it is my duty, one I have inherited from my father and my grandfather. They are unable to. They are quite old. It is up to me. I shall take back what belongs to Serbia. I'm going there because all my family was killed at Jasenovac concentration camp during World War II. I come from Banja. My origins are there. I grew up in Srem. Understand? I'm going there just because of that, because I know what they are doing -- what they have done during the war from 1941 to 1945." "How old are you?" "Sixty-three. " "And you feel able?" "I feel great, great. And I am going there with resolve and enthusiasm. They do not know any fear. They have said they are only of their own desire to end the tragedy of the endangered Serbs as soon as possible and of their own willingness to help them in it."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The accused says he's very pleased that this has been shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Registrar, could we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P392, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The next seven videos deal with the topic: Instigation, hate speech. The next video is 6006A. It has the ERN number V000-2125. It's about six minutes and 15 seconds' long, and we got it from the RTV Belgrade interview with Branka Karac [phoen]. Sorry, I correct. We received this videotape from Natasha Kandic on the 1st of April, 1996. The content is also published in Mr. Seselj's -- one of Mr. Seselj's books. You have it on the outline. I don't read it out now. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Tell us, you have already talked a lot about inter-ethnic relations. Tell us, in this context, how do you think the Kosovo issue can be resolved? "The communist measures currently enforced on territory of Kosovo and Metohija have given certain results, but in the long run they cannot provide the right solution. That is why we advocate much more radical measures to be taken in Kosovo and Metohija. We advocate immediate cessation and financial aid to Siptar ethnic minority, and we have recently learned from the regime press that every day in Kosovo-Metohija to the Siptars $1.500.000 from the fund for assistance to the underdeveloped republics and provinces was sent, these means were mainly used to finance their excessive procreation, expulsion of Serbs from this vital historical territory of ours. We advocate abolishing the university in the Siptar language as well all the cultural institutions which were subsidized from the state budget. "We have nothing against the Siptar minority having all this, but they should finance it themselves with their own funds. Furthermore, we advocate immediate termination of production in all factories that make no profit due to silent Siptar boycotts of production. These people should simply be fired, and then they should find their own way around. If need be, we will provide all of them with passports, but we will no longer finance them for doing nothing. "Next, we think that all military and police academies, a military institution, is not directly involved in the command over certain army districts as well as certain state institutions should be moved to Kosovo and Metohija, which would result in the moving of tens of thousands of officers, non-commissioned officers, policemen, civil servants, their families and all their structure to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. This would significantly change the total ethnic picture of the population in Kosovo and Metohija. Furthermore, we advocate opening mines, coal mines in Kosovo and Metohija immediately, and wherever possible, the building of thermal-electric power plants. Thanks to huge resources of coal in Kosovo-Metohija Serbia could become one of the largest exporters of electrical energy in Europe. Where would we build these thermal power plants? In places most densely populated by the Siptars, where their fertile land is located, where their houses are. We would be doing the same to them what they did to the Serbs since the war. "The world would not be able to accuse us of anything. If they say, 'You're displacing the Siptars,' we answer, 'Well, we have to displace them. We're building thermal-electric power plants there.' The thermal-electric power plants are the condition for brining social standards and a higher living standard. We cannot move forward, economically speaking, if we don't do that. This is done all over the world, and nobody can object to that. We pay them fair financial compensation, and you know how much it is, bearing in mind the permanent inflation we've got, and no one can do anything about this. "Arrests of the demonstrators prevention of their political organisation and so on are measures that can give results for a short term, but have no effect in the long run. The true key to solving the Siptar -- to stopping the Siptar separatist rebellion lies in undertaking economic measures. They should be forced by economic measures to give up their separatism and a large number of them would then move out from Kosovo because they would not be able to live if we stopped financing them. Furthermore, we advocate -- "Yes, but don't you think you would be violating their rights because of this? "What rights? Let them find their way around. Let them find their way around. Let them work. Produce. Let them find their way as best as possible. In a free society, it is understood that everyone is able to take care of themselves. Why would we -- is it their right to be financed by us? That has been the case up 'till now but it will no longer be so. "Furthermore, we advocate that the 360.000 Albanian immigrants who came to Serbia from Albania from the 6th of April 1941 until today be urgently expelled from Serbia along with all their offspring handed over to the United Nations High Commissioner of Refugees. They are so many incomparably wealthy and bigger countries so they can take of them. Let them do that for a change, show their humanity. Why would we, the Serbs, be the ones to constantly prove our humanity, just to have these Albanians immigrants return the favour by stabbing us in the back. "Furthermore, and this would be one of the key measures as well, we are in favour of pronouncing a stretch of some 20 to 50 kilometres along the Albanian an area of strategic importance for Serbia and having all the members of the Siptar national minority move to other parts of Yugoslavia for the purpose of protecting Serbian national sovereignty and territorial integrity and for which they would be given a fair financial compensation. For example, they could be moved to the territories of the present Croatia and Slovenia as it turned out that they loved them there most, and that they would be thrilled to accept this proposal of ours, that they would welcome them with open arms. When proposing this, I'm bearing in mind the fact that for quite some time it has been proved that the true centre of Siptar separatist rebellion is neither Pristina or Tirana, but Zagreb and Ljubljana, and all the farm land in this stretch should be given over to the army. The army would be reviving agricultural production until conditions are met to populate the area with Serb inhabitants on a more massive scale, all Serbs and members of other national minorities on the territory of Serbia who are loyal to the Serbian state, we would allow them to go there. We would give them this farm land free of charge. They would renew agricultural production there, they form joint stock companies in places, and this would solve the problem of the Siptar separatist rebellion. Otherwise, the Siptars would win in the long run. Time is on their side unless these key economic measures, these radical measures are undertaken."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before giving the floor to Mr. Seselj, Mr. Prosecutor, could you tell us what exactly the relevance of this document is? It is connected to a presidential electoral campaign. Obviously, the topic here is Kosovo. However, I believe I've already seen clips, these clips, or excerpts of this clip when -- of the Oberschall expert witness was heard. Haven't we already seen at least excerpts of this video?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: At the moment, I'm not in the position to tell you. If have already seen, I wouldn't exclude it, but you haven't seen this in its entirety. And the relevance is, as I mentioned, that we have it under the topic of instigation, hate speech. It is against Kosovo. This is true, Kosovo is not part of the indictment, but the date is the 6th of December, 1990, when this interview took place, and for the Prosecution it demonstrates a typical approach of Mr. Seselj to other ethnicities, even if it's against Albanians in this case, which is not part of the indictment, but we have similar quotes from him in his books against the Croats and against other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have four matters to raise. First, Mr. Mussemeyer is using hate speech here, because he says that I am speaking against Kosovo. No, I am speaking in favour of Kosovo, in the best interests of Kosovo. But he is burdened by anti-Serb hatred and considers that Kosovo is not Serbian, because he comes from a country that's already recognised this independence of Kosovo proclaimed in that way, so it's normal that he behaves in that way. And it's only the countries that are toppling international rights and have already done so. There are not even 30 of them yet. That's the first point I wanted to raise. The second point is this: I'm very proud with that speech of mine, even today. The third point is that as far as this trial is concerned, the most important fact is that this clip was sent by Natasha Kandic. The fourth point: This is a clip which dates to 1990, and that is as far removed from the period incorporated in the indictment. And the fifth thing I wish to say is this: The Prosecution still has not amended the indictment with incriminations dealing with Kosovo and Metohija. Why is it getting ahead of itself? Why hasn't it put that in the indictment yet? What does all that mean? And Mr. Mussemeyer says this is similar to what I say about the Croats and Muslims. Well, why doesn't he find that similar -- similarity and offer that up as evidence? Why would you do guesswork, as the Trial Chamber? You have my speech, my programme speech, about the question of the Siptar separatist rebellion in Kosovo and Metohija could be solved, and the prosecutor is making you speculate and do guess work saying I have similar speeches about Croats and Muslims. Well, let him find those similar speeches then. He can't, because they don't exist. All problems in the Former Yugoslavia and each and every problem is specific in its nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber deliberated on this matter, that is to say, whether this evidence should be admitted and whether we should have a number for this evidence. Judge Lattanzi had a dissident [as interpreted] opinion, but to the majority we have decided that this document should be admitted -- this video should be admitted into evidence, and this is why I'm going to ask Madam Registrar to give it a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P393, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Next video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: One short comment. I think Mr. Seselj should not always refer to the nationality of the members of the Trial Chamber. We also have a free opinion, and it's not that I'm from a specific country that I hate Serbs. This is the comment I wanted to make, because it's constantly inferred that members of the Trial Chamber from specific countries hate specific ethnicities, which is not true. We have our own opinion and our own free will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer, I completely support what you just said. It doesn't mean that because one comes from a country that has recognised Kosovo, that that means that that person agrees with the decisions made by its own country. So I believe that Mr. Seselj should refrain from mentioning nationalities of parties involved in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The next video is again under the topic: Hate speeches instigation. It has the 65 ter number 6015D. The ERN number is V000-1507. It's 25 seconds' long, and it's from the video clip "Without Incision and Without Anaesthesia." You already saw videos from this clip. I'm not in a position now to tell you where we got it from. Yes, I can see this. It was handed over to the ICTY on the 27th of August, 1998, by embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina in The Hague. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] " ... and it's high time that we Serbs put an end to all this and send an ultimatum to these federal authorities that have no way of disarming the paramilitary units. Either they do so very soon or we, the Serbian Chetniks, will start disarming the Croats ourselves, and then there will certainly be a lot more bloodshed than if the army disarms them."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that once again the problem of relevance crops up here. And as far as time is concerned, because this is a May 1991 speech, and also of substance. I think that this is my most peace-loving speech, and the Prosecutor has qualified this as being hate speech. I'm asking for the disarmament of paramilitary formations by the legal army of the SFRY, which was the Yugoslav People's Army, and I am pointing out what would happen if they do not do so. So I can't be more peace-loving than I was there. I don't know where the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to ask Madam Registrar to give a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P394, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip bears the 65 ter number 6025F. It has the ERN number V000-4745. It's about 43 seconds' long. It's a report made by the Serbian Television, and we received this clip from a protected witness. The transcript of this appears also as -- it's outlined in Mr. Seselj's book about "Milan Panic Must Fall" is the title. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection before we see the clip. I have an objection to make before we see the footage. The Prosecutor said that this clip was given him by a protected witness, whereas here it says that this clip was seized from a man, who not on pain of his own life wanted to be a Prosecution witness or a Trial Chamber witness, a Court witness, all he wanted to be was a Defence witness, to make the information correct. Somebody sees the clip, which means that somebody searched his flat and found this footage. It wasn't that this person handed it over. At least that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, was it handed down to you or was it seized, which is not the same thing, of course?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: It was not seized. It was given to the Prosecution voluntarily, and it's not the only one which was given voluntarily. Nothing was seized, nothing was done by force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you're telling us that this document was given to the Prosecution voluntarily. What is really important is what we see in the video, mainly. Let's look at the video now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Mr. President, what is more relevant for us, what it says on the official OTP document or what Mr. Mussemeyer says? We have seen that his memory is not always in the best order. And this is an official OTP document where it says that the tape was seized, so we can't take Mr. Mussemeyer at his word when his memory seems to have failed the test many times before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's look at the video clip, and I would like to ask the Prosecution to check. There seems to be a difference between a document that would be given voluntarily and a document which would have been seized. You're telling us the document was given to you. You will tell us later. It is not urgent. Maybe you can check and tell us after the break, what it is, since Mr. Seselj is noting a contradiction here. But let's look at the video now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "General Staff to immediately ask the separatist government in Skopje and to reinstate the Yugoslav government authorities there. If one thinks that the army is not capable of carrying out this task at the moment because of its engagement in many other areas and because of the difficult international circumstances, we demand the division of the Macedonian territory between Serbia, Albania, Greece, and Bulgaria. "What Bosnia-Herzegovina is concerned, Dr. Seselj believes that for Bosnia, the same solution as for Macedonia applies. "Bosnia and Herzegovina will never be an independent and sovereign state. It will rather bathe in rivers of blood."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Firstly, as far as Macedonia is concerned, I assume that the Prosecution is proving the state of consciousness. But the Prosecution must know that Macedonia was never an independent state until it was under American patronage that it seceded from Yugoslavia in 1992. So that is not something that is god-given and must be preserved at all costs. Secondly, Macedonia today is called "Macedonia" only in that portion which was liberated by the Serbian Army in 1912. The other part of Macedonia, which was liberated by Bulgaria, there have not been any Macedonians there for a long time. And the part of Macedonia liberated by the Greek Army, for a long time there were no Macedonians there either. So the Macedonian nation was proclaimed under the communist regime of Yugoslavia. It is not recognised today either by Bulgaria or Greece. But the Prosecutor does not know that. Of course, he need not know everything. Now, as far as this other clip is concerned, it's too brief an extract to be understood. However, these words seem to be providential. In February 1992, I say that there can be no talk of the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that Bosnia will bathe in blood if secession is allowed to take place. And Bosnia did indeed bathe in blood because the world factors did not listen to me. It would have been wiser for them if they listened to me on time. It didn't never become an independent state and will never become an independent state. This Bosnia-Herzegovina of today, which is occupied in the true sense of the world, is not an independent state. It is a territory under occupation. We have an international governor administering Bosnia-Herzegovina, and now we have this man Licek [phoen]. Many of them succeeded each other from [indiscernible] and so on, and even that other international, Adi Asdoun [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Registrar, could we have a number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P395, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we proceed, Mr. Seselj, you have made some objections for the matters of time. You say this video is not within the scope of the indictment, when it comes to dates, since you've made some time references. You are stating some of the matters, and I will read paragraph 8 of the indictment so we can all know what it's about. Paragraph 8(a) begins as follows: "The joint criminal enterprise, a force mentioned, came into existence before August 1st, 1991, and continued at least until December of 1995." Then it reads as follows: "Vojislav Seselj participated in the joint criminal enterprise until September of 1993, when he had a conflict with Slobodan Milosevic." What is important here is that the criminal enterprise -- joint criminal enterprise began before the 1st of August, 1991; 1990, 1989, we don't really know exactly, but here in the indictment, we do see the word "before." This is what I wanted to note. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what it says -- where it says "before the 1st of August, 1991," that provision has nothing to do with law. It's only the 1st of August that can have any connection with law -- anything -- where it says "before," that is speculation, which is not allowed in law. But I'd like to remind you of the first indictment raised against me, where it says that I was a participant in the joint criminal enterprise from February 1991. And then when I testified during the Slobodan Milosevic trial, it transpired that he was a participant since August 1991. I, from February to August, was the only participant in that joint criminal enterprise. I joined myself in that enterprise, and then all the others joined me in August. So this is all nebulous, constructed and construed by the Prosecutor. When you say "before the 1st of August," that in law means nothing, absolutely nothing. It means since the time of my birth. There's no guesswork and speculation in the realm of law, nor can any incrimination be based on guesswork, and Prosecutors and courts must be precise. If they lack precision, well, it's like somebody saying that I raped an unknown girl. You bring in three witnesses to testify that I raped an unknown girl. They don't know what the girl's name is, they don't know where she's from, or where she is, nor did they see it with their own eyes. So that's the same type of formulation when you say "before August the 1st." If you accept that formulation, that's all right, but I have to object to it and put my views to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much for your comments. They are noted in the transcript for today's day, and I will myself check as to what you just mentioned. In the first indictment, the month of February was there, but then it was changed to the month of August. So I will check this later. It is time for the break. We will take a 20-minute break and we will resume in 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed, and we will continue watching videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I come back to the last video we showed. You asked me to check if it was seized or given voluntarily. Our record says that it was submitted by the protected witness on the 19th of September, 2003. So the information in the record -- in the list I gave you is not exact. It was not seized. It was submitted, and that was voluntarily. And what I want to comment on is why it is important for the Prosecution. Mr. Seselj, and this is not the only occasion where he mentioned rivers of blood. If you see the date of this video, which was February 1992, and what happened later, it's up to you to make your own conclusion. Those are my comments to this. The next video is 65 ter number 128A. It has the ERN number V000-5022. It's about a bit more than 30 seconds' long, and the Prosecution received this from the IRD studio from Vienna the 1st of February, 2004.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina is the direct introduction into that war, and stimulation of the conflict. The Serbian will never recognise the independence of this new jamahirija and will never give up its territories. It will set the bounds and preserve them. This is a matter of survival, do or die. As far as this alleged lifting of the sanctions against Serbia is concerned, I believe that they have not been lifted, actually. This is just some sort of a promise that the sanctions will be lifted if Serbia agrees to the ultimatum."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm waiting for you to let me know that the translation has been completed, as suggested by Judge Lattanzi. This is not problematic for me, this video. I don't mind it being admitted into evidence. But what is problematic is the previous statement by Mr. Mussemeyer. He says that I speak about floods of -- rivers of blood in other places, and he must show where and when. He must understand that this is a poetic expression. In Serbian literature, it is frequently used, "rivers of blood spilled for the freedom of the Serbian people." He doesn't understand that. I don't mind that he doesn't understand, but I do mind when he's imprecise. He can't say there are other such statements. Where is it? In law, you can't say there's more of this. You have to say where and when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can we have a number, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P395, Your Honours. I apologise. 396.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Next clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The next clip will be the 65 ter number 6062C. It has the ERN number V000-0710. It's about one minute and 47 seconds' long, and this tape was sent to the OTP from the Embassy of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Brussels on 18th of March, 1996, on the request of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I believe that today you have also had an opportunity to hear the news that Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska announced that a very, very strong Muslim offensive started this morning on Vlasic and Majevica. Do you consider this to be the deciding battle for them, or are they testing the strength of the Serb Army once again? "Well, we are expecting that -- we were expecting that offensive. I did not know where they would strike first, but it was up in the air. That was known, and that could not have been avoided. It was well known the Muslims used this peace time to rearm and reorganise themselves for the forthcoming conflicts. In this case, the Serbs must retaliate with force, without stopping. They should not allow any ceasefires. Now we must finish off the Muslims on all fronts. The 5th Corps around Vlasic, Trebave, on Majevica, wherever they attacked, they must be finished off, and then they will never attack again. You know, it can happen to a smart man to be bitten by the snake, but if the same snake bites him twice, then he should question his intelligence. If the snake bites him once, he should crash its head so she can never bite him again. This time, no attention should be paid to pressures and threats from the outside. There is nothing else we need to wait for. Now we have to definitely finish up with the Muslims."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here again the question of time relevance and substantial relevance arises. This recording is from the 20th of March, 1995. This is two years after I had clashed with Slobodan Milosevic. I abandoned the joint criminal enterprise, as the Prosecution calls it. These may be the remnants of my previous alleged participation in the joint criminal enterprise, so this is very strange. Now, what is hate speech here? Clearly, we say I'm referring to the destruction of the Muslim army. I'm saying where, at Majevica, which is a mountain, Vlasic is a mountain, Trebave is a mountain. I didn't say that the Muslim need to be destroyed in Sarajevo, in Tuzla, but the Muslim army needs to be destroyed. As in war, when the Germans attacked over there, they were destroyed over there, they won over there, they were defeated in the Ardens and so on, it's the same sort of inference. The enemy in the war is referred to by his ethnicity, "We have defeated the Germans, we have destroyed the Germans." The Prosecution is trying to use a trick. They don't wish to define it, but it can be inferred. It is a foggy example of a hate speech which the Prosecution is not able to explain to this day, what they mean when they talk about hate speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unanimously, the Trial Chamber decided to dismiss this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the last two videos deal with the topic "History of Chetnik Movement." The first one has the 65 ter number 6021G. The ERN number is V000-3780. The clip is about two minutes' long, and the OTP received this video from the Croatian government in 2002. It's an interview broadcast to "TV Politika."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Don't you think that the iconography which could be seen a few days ago when the memorial service was held for Draza Mihajlovic, and which included black heads, skulls and bones, long hairs, does that iconography repel people, particularly young people and people who have already lived through all that? After all, we should keep in mind that the SUBNOR/Federal Association of World War II veterans or that veteran organisation counts 600- 700.000 people, and those people have once already lived through all that. Yes, and that veteran organisation is, it seems, continues to be getting bigger. They just won't die. There are always more and more of them, and I don't know how long that is going to last for. And as for the iconography, I think that it should bother no one. "Firstly, black flags are the main hallmark of the Chetnik movement already from the times. "Yes, I know that. That was inherited from the Serbian guerrilla units and the like. After all, they were very effective. You know when those Chetniks units with black flags show up in places where there are Ustashas, Ustashas run for their lives. Whereas if 50 Chetniks show up, Croats think there are 10.000 of them, then they flee in panic. For example, a small group of Chetniks showed up at a village near Zadar about two months ago, approximately, and a rumour spread through Zadar that I was with that unit. If we had decided to take Zadar that night, and by sheer coincidence the power failed in Zadar. The panic then took over and all the Ustasha oriented people left their homes towards the harbour and went on board ships and boats. Those who did not have a boat with an engine went on board boats with oars just to push off to open sea expecting the arrival of Chetniks. Thus the Croats, first of all, showed that their conscience is not clear. On the other hand, the Chetnik tradition, which is full of heroic acts, heroic feats, is also very effective in this war which is being waged against the new Ustasha state."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there are serious problem because of an inadequate translation. I think those are the serious problems because of inadequate translation of this clip. This reference is to the Ustasha-inclined population of Zadar. Now, whether it says "Ustasha" or "Croats," so the translation does not correspond to the substance of what I said. Of course, there's also a problem because the interviewer is overlapping with me, who knows the Serb language well, can make a distinction. Those who don't speak Serbian well cannot know what each one of us said. So then there's the question of relevance. It is June 1991. Actually, it's an anecdote that was recounted. The Croats had heard that Seselj appeared with the Chetniks close to Zadar and they boarded boats and fled to the islands. In Bosnia, a similar anecdote was spread: As there was a shortage of oil, sugar, and milk, in a Muslim town, in a shop, somebody wrote in capitals, "sugar is coming," "stize secer," and somebody understood it meant "Seselj is coming," and there was panic and everyone fled. So here's an anecdote that I'm telling in the studio, and the Prosecution is using it as hate speech. It's similar to the anecdote about slaughtering with rusty spoons, shoehorns, because the Chetniks were always said that they were slaughterers. I said, yes, instead of using a knife, we now use a rusty shoehorn, so one cannot tell whether the victim died due to the slaughtering or to the infection because of the rust. So somebody who doesn't know Serbian well cannot see that it is an anecdote. He just wishes to pursue his goals, without consulting anyone. This is the problem of one-dimensional personalities which are numerous in the OTP. The Serb people describe such people as beach heads, as empty heads. When someone has such an empty head, he sticks to his one line of thought and he doesn't develop his thoughts, there's no feeling for different views. So one-dimensional personalities are familiar from social psychology, and we know what kind of characteristics such personalities have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber unanimously, once again, decides to admit this video clip and would like a number, please, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will become Exhibit number P397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think we have one last video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: In fact, we have. It appears as 65 ter number 6072A. The ERN number is V000-1508. It's about four minutes and 20 seconds' long. It's from the 23rd of June, 1997, and it is an interview with a Slavko Aleksic. Slavko Aleksic was appointed vojvoda by Mr. Seselj in the order I quoted already this morning, number 124. He is number 1, and he was during the war in Sarajevo. The OTP received this tape from the AID in Sarajevo on the 27th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Politics created the borders in this war. Maybe it was supposed to be like that, maybe not. History will be the judge of that. However, the people erased those borders." "Yes. For the people on this and the other side of the Drina River, the borders never existed. Drina should represent the backbone of the Serbian people. It is our task to finish what sparked immediately after the decapitation of the immortal Prince Lazar at Kosovo Polje. That spark initiated the first Serbian rebellion, the growth of national consciousness, unification. The final goal of all that should be the creation of a Serbian national state and the final solution to the eternal Serbian national question. "The cry of the Serbian patriots going to death was, 'unification or death,' or, 'freedom or death.' Without the unification and freedom, we would be left with the other choice, and that is death, in a national and a general sense. And what is going on now? You know what the answer of Croatia to the Serbian national issue was, as well as Slovenian, Muslim, and Macedonian answers. "The people of Serbia are anxiously awaiting for the Siptars, a derogatory term for Albanians, answer; that is, Siptar's national answer to the Serbian national issue. They are hoping that the national answer of the Montenegrins to the Serbian national issue will be positive. Until the moment when the Serbs establish a unified Serbian state on integrated Serbian territory, and until the Serbian national question is solved, I am afraid that they will keep on getting killed in these wars and that their territory will be further disintegrated and so on. We are a small people, but we had many opportunities in our history to become big. Unfortunately, we did not use those opportunities. Let's remind ourselves of the year 1918 and the end of World War I, and the London Agreement, and the borders of the Serbian state along the axis Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica. However, the romantic desire of our poets and politicians on triune people titled the balance. Ante Pavelic killed this romanticism in Jasenovac. He drew the Serbian borders through the Serbian throats using the Ustasha knives and fenced it in with Jadovni, Golubinjaca, Jasenovac and so on. "I, as a Chetnik vojvoda or duke, and all those with me, shall never give up the idea of the borders of the Serbian country along the axis Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica. The French waited for 47 years for the Germans to give them back Alsace and Lorraine and succeeded. We did not lose Knin, Eastern Slavonia, Western Slavonia, and Srem in the course of a battle. We lost them during peace. Someone gave them away, someone handed them over. The same is happening with Serbian Sarajevo. I had to move my family out of Serbian Sarajevo, but I do hope that one day, I may not be around to see it, we will be back in Serbian Sarajevo, in our Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that a Serbian Chetnik vojvoda, Slavko Aleksic, is speaking intelligently, and in my opinion this statement has nothing to be said against it. But, again, the question of relevance arises. It is dated the 23rd of June, 1997, so the temporal relevance arises. You have similar statements from this year, too, people who are very close to me, who are Chetnik vojvodas or senior officials of the Serbian Radical Party. What is being proven through this? Secondly, what does the Prosecution truly want to say with this? We have a problem. It may be purely a problem of translation.
